items.headline: Red Flag Warning issued June 26 at 9:07AM AKDT until June 27 at 3:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The National Weather Service in Fairbanks has issued a Red Flag
Warning for lightning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday
afternoon to 3 AM AKDT Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Lower Yukon River, Middle Yukon Valley, Lower
Yukon and Innoko Valleys and Upper Kuskokwim Valley.

* TIMING...From 1 PM Friday afternoon to 3 AM AKDT Saturday.

* THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE INDEX...Numerous

* WINDS...Northwest 8 to 15 mph.

* HUMIDITY...As low as 35 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the mid 70s to near 80.
items.areas: Lower Yukon River; Middle Yukon Valley; Lower Yukon and Innoko Valleys; Upper Kuskokwim Valley
items.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that conditions are occurring or will
occur which could lead to the development of large and dangerous
fires. It is directed toward fire agencies, and through them, to
the public.

Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the
field of this Red Flag Warning.

items.headline: Red Flag Warning issued June 26 at 9:02AM AKDT until June 27 at 12:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The National Weather Service in Fairbanks has issued a Red Flag
Warning for lightning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday to
12 AM Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Yukon Flats and Fortymile Country.

* TIMING...From 1 PM Friday to 12 AM Saturday.

* THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE INDEX...Scattered

* WINDS...Northeast 6 to 12 mph.

* HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the upper 70s to near 80.

* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected due to
scattered thunderstorms.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued June 25 at 1:40PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
White Mountains, Fairbanks, Chatanika and Chena Basins, Parks Hwy
corridor from Fairbanks to Healy, Denali National Park

A long-duration period of moderate rain is anticipated to start on
Saturday evening and continue through Monday. This could impact a
large portion of the Interior with a particular focus near Denali
National Park.

Return intervals indicate this as a 1 in 5 year to a 1 in 10 year
event.  We are continuing to monitor and will provide updates on
